subject: FinLytics — post-demo follow-up: data handling, logging & support access
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finlytics.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinLytics — follow-up: data handling & support access (recap + asks)

Hi Amit / Priya — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and a short list of asks so we can move to a technical deep-dive next week.

Recap (high level)
- Primary concern: PII handling for transaction metadata and customer identifiers (fields marked as PII in your data model).
- Data residency: must remain in US for production; EU option desired for APAC/EU customers later.
- Retention: default retention for logs & usage tokens; you flagged regulatory need for 12+ months for a subset of audit logs.
- Support access: you asked for least-privilege RBAC, documented break-glass flows, and audit logs for any support sessions.

Attachments included (initial evidence)
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf — high-level SOC 2 controls and scope.
- support_access_matrix.xlsx — proposed roles & permitted operations for support.
- dpa-draft.docx — our standard DPA template (editable).

Clarifications / answers we committed to deliver
1) How logs are stored, retained, and what they contain (request IDs, request metadata, and whether raw prompt/response text is retained by default).
2) Key management options (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed) and support for HSM.
3) RBAC: mapping of Redwood roles to least-priv privilege for your operators + how break-glass is authorized & logged.
4) Whether support sessions can be scoped to a dedicated test environment or tenant (yes in Dedicated/Private; we'll detail options).

Next steps (asks for FinLytics)
- Please confirm whether your retention requirement (12 months) applies to all request logs or only to audit logs for security/suspect events.
- Provide a short list of the first three support engineers we should pre-authorize for break-glass (names + corporate email).
- Share any internal compliance questionnaire XLS you want us to populate before the technical deep-dive.

Proposed timeline
- Technical deep-dive (solutions + infra): Wed 2026-08-11 or Thu 2026-08-12. Rishi to lead.
- Deliver updated RBAC matrix and KMS options: by Fri 2026-08-06.

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and Rishi will send the RBAC + logs proposal tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FinLytics — follow-up: data handling & support access (recap + asks)

Thanks Sofia — useful recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock the deep-dive: 

- Retention: when you say "logs & usage tokens", do logs include the full prompt & response by default? We need any PII stripped from routine logs. Audit logs for security investigations can retain more, but we need to understand the separation and how we can enforce retention policies per-log-class.
- Encryption: confirm support for CMK in AWS KMS and whether Redwood supports external HSMs for key wrapping. Also, are encryption keys rotated automatically or on-demand?
- Break-glass: need a clear attestation that break-glass access is only allowed after two-step approval (customer code + email confirmation) and that all actions are captured with immutable audit trails.

Also — do you have a sample support runbook that shows the typical limited-access troubleshooting steps (so we can compare to our internal playbooks)? If possible, include the version for Dedicated/private deployments vs hosted.

We can do the deep-dive Wed 8/11 afternoon PT. Priya and I will be there.

—Amit

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinLytics — follow-up: data handling & support access (recap + asks)

Hi Amit / Priya — quick technical notes below; happy to cover in the deep-dive and share a longer design doc ahead of the meeting.

Retention & logging
- Default: request metadata (request id, model, timestamps, routing) retained 90 days. Raw prompt + response are NOT stored by default for hosted customers unless "logging enabled" is turned on for evals/QA. For Dedicated/Private you can choose to disable prompt logging entirely.
- Audit logs: can be configured to retain 13 months (396 days) for events flagged as security/audit. We support per-log-class retention policies (you can pick retention per stream).
- Separation: logs are written to distinct buckets/streams (operational vs audit). Access controls restrict who can read each stream; automation enforces retention lifecycle.

KMS & encryption
- Customer-managed keys supported: AWS KMS CMKs and AWS CloudHSM for Dedicated/private deployments. We also support integration with external HSM via standard key-wrapping (bring-your-own-key).
- Key rotation: supported on-demand via API; we can also schedule automated rotation (customer-configurable cadence). Re-encryption of stored objects is sandboxed to avoid wide rekey windows.

RBAC / break-glass
- RBAC model: roles -> permissions -> resource scoping. Attached is a draft RBAC matrix showing Redwood roles mapped to least privilege for support tasks (see redwood-rbac-matrix.csv).
- Break-glass flow (summary):
  1) Customer raises a break-glass request via console or signed DocuSign form;
  2) Two-factor approval: required from the named customer approver + a delegated security officer at FinLytics;
  3) Temporary scoped credentials issued (timebox + limited endpoints);
  4) All CLI/API actions during the session are immutably logged and pushed to a customer-only audit bucket.
- We log session transcripts (metadata + request ids) but we can mask or exclude raw PII fields per tenant policy.

Support scoping & attestation
- For Dedicated/private, we can provision a sandbox tenant for troubleshooting that contains synthetic data (recommended for incident reproduction).
- We can provide a written attestation that any accidental access will be investigated, and remediation steps will be performed; that attestation can be part of the DPA addendum.

Deliverables by EOD Thu 2026-08-06
- Updated RBAC matrix (redwood-rbac-matrix.csv).
- A short runbook (PDF) showing typical limited-access troubleshooting steps for Hosted vs Dedicated.
- Link to SOC2 summary (already attached).

(Attachment: redwood-rbac-matrix.csv (csv))

Happy to expand on any of these. Will also paste a short sample runbook to this thread before the deep-dive.

Thanks,

- Can you include a short table of what "masking" means in practice (field-level vs tokenization vs hashing) and any limits on search/forensics when masking is applied?
- We require a short list of Redwood personnel who could be authorized for break-glass (name, role, country, background-check status). Please mark which personnel would need additional approvals.
- We will send our compliance questionnaire by EOD today. Could you populate the sections on encryption, logs retention, and incident response?

We can confirm Wed 2026-08-11 14:00 PT for the deep-dive. Priya and Amit will join; I’ll loop in our infra lead if needed.
